name: New Zealand
title: New Zealand Political Compass Test 2026 | CoreOpinion
desc: Where do you stand in New Zealand politics? 70 statements to see your alignment with National, Labour, the Greens, ACT, NZ First and Te Pāti Māori, plus your framing bias.
keywords: New Zealand political compass, voting helper NZ, NZ election 2026, which party to vote NZ, political test NZ, National, Labour, Greens, ACT, NZ First, Te Pati Maori

desc.en: Your answers most closely match the National Party. You support tax cuts, fiscal responsibility, infrastructure investment, and a strong focus on law and order.
Your answers most closely match the Labour Party. You support social safety nets, investments in public healthcare and education, and state-backed climate action.
Your answers most closely match the Green Party. You place high importance on aggressive carbon emission cuts, environmental protection, wealth redistribution, and social justice.
Your answers most closely match ACT New Zealand. You support classic liberal policies: a minimal state, tax simplification, deregulation, and individual liberties.
Your answers most closely match New Zealand First. You support moderate protectionism, nationalist policies, stricter immigration controls, and support for seniors.
Your answers most closely match Te Pāti Māori. You support indigenous Māori rights and self-determination, environmental protection, and progressive social justice policies.
Your answers do not align strongly with any single party. You hold a mixed, centrist or pragmatic stance across various political issues.

bank.q: The principles of the Treaty of Waitangi should be defined by referendum, not the courts.
bank.ctx: The Treaty of Waitangi (1840) is NZ's founding agreement with Māori. This supports having its principles defined by a public referendum rather than the courts.

bank.q: Redefining the Treaty by referendum is an attack on Māori rights and the founding agreement itself.
bank.ctx: This argues redefining the Treaty by referendum attacks Māori rights and the founding agreement itself.

bank.q: Co-governance arrangements that give Māori a special role in public services have gone too far.
bank.ctx: 'Co-governance' gives Māori a shared role in running some public services. This argues it has gone too far.

bank.q: Co-governance honours the Treaty partnership and should be expanded, not rolled back.
bank.ctx: This defends co-governance as honouring the Treaty partnership and wants it expanded, not cut back.

bank.q: Māori language and culture should be actively promoted across New Zealand life.
bank.ctx: 'Te reo' is the Māori language. This supports actively promoting Māori language and culture across New Zealand life.

bank.q: Pushing te reo and Māori culture into everything is divisive and should stop.
bank.ctx: This argues pushing Māori language and culture into everything is divisive and should stop.

bank.q: New Zealand should finally introduce a capital gains tax.
bank.ctx: A capital gains tax taxes profit made from selling assets like property or shares. New Zealand has none; this supports finally introducing one.

bank.q: A capital gains tax would punish savers and investors and drive money out of New Zealand.
bank.ctx: This argues a capital gains tax would punish savers and investors and drive money out of the country.

bank.q: The wealthiest New Zealanders should pay significantly more tax.
bank.ctx: This supports significantly higher taxes on the wealthiest New Zealanders.

bank.q: Higher taxes on the successful just drive talent and capital across the Tasman.
bank.ctx: This argues higher taxes on the successful just drive talent and money to Australia ('across the Tasman').

bank.q: Public health must stay well funded and free, and privatisation resisted.
bank.ctx: This wants public healthcare kept well funded and free, resisting privatisation.

bank.q: More private provision and competition would cut the waiting lists crippling the public system.
bank.ctx: This argues more private provision and competition would cut the public system's crippling waiting lists.

bank.q: Government should build state housing on a large scale to fix the crisis.
bank.ctx: 'State housing' is government-owned rental housing. This supports building it on a large scale to fix the housing crisis.

bank.q: The housing fix is freeing up land and cutting red tape, not more state building.
bank.ctx: This argues the fix is freeing up land and cutting red tape, not more government building.

bank.q: Gangs and violent crime need a crackdown: tougher sentences and more police powers.
bank.ctx: This supports a crackdown on gangs and violent crime: tougher sentences and more police powers.

bank.q: Locking more people up has never cut crime; addressing poverty and addiction does.
bank.ctx: This argues locking more people up hasn't cut crime, and that tackling poverty and addiction does.

bank.q: Young repeat offenders behind ram raids need real consequences, including boot camps.
bank.ctx: 'Ram raids' are smash-and-grab robberies, often by youths. This supports real consequences for young repeat offenders, including boot camps.

bank.q: Boot camps for children are proven to fail; these kids need support, not punishment.
bank.ctx: This argues boot camps for children are proven to fail and that these kids need support, not punishment.

bank.q: New Zealand must cut emissions faster, including from agriculture.
bank.ctx: This supports cutting emissions faster, including from farming, which is NZ's biggest emissions source.

bank.q: Punishing farmers with emissions rules threatens the backbone of the economy for tiny global gain.
bank.ctx: This argues emissions rules on farmers threaten the backbone of the economy for tiny global benefit.

bank.q: Immigration levels are too high and are straining housing and infrastructure.
bank.ctx: This argues immigration levels are too high and are straining housing and infrastructure.

bank.q: Immigration brings the skills and workers New Zealand needs, and should not be cut.
bank.ctx: This is the pro-immigration view: that migrants bring skills and workers New Zealand needs.

bank.q: Multiculturalism has been good for New Zealand.
bank.ctx: This holds that multiculturalism has been good for New Zealand.

bank.q: Mass immigration and multiculturalism are eroding New Zealand’s character.
bank.ctx: This argues mass immigration and multiculturalism are eroding New Zealand's character.

bank.q: Islam is not compatible with New Zealand values.
bank.ctx: This argues Islam clashes with New Zealand values. Supporters cite integration concerns; critics call it religious prejudice.

bank.q: Muslim New Zealanders are full members of society, and their faith deserves equal respect.
bank.ctx: This holds that Muslim New Zealanders are full members of society whose faith deserves equal respect.

bank.q: Some races are simply more intelligent or capable than others.
bank.ctx: This is a statement of racial supremacism — the belief that some races are inherently more intelligent or capable than others. Mainstream science rejects it, and it is historically tied to ideologies like Nazism and systems like apartheid.

bank.q: There is no hierarchy of races; the idea is pseudo-science with a shameful history.
bank.ctx: This is the principle of human equality: that no race is inherently smarter or more capable, and that the idea of a racial hierarchy is discredited pseudo-science with a shameful history.

bank.q: Trans New Zealanders should be able to change their legal gender by self-identification.
bank.ctx: This supports transgender rights: the view that people should be able to have the law recognise the gender they identify as, without needing medical approval.

bank.q: Biological sex is a reality the law should not let a declaration override.
bank.ctx: This is the gender-critical view: that biological sex is a fixed fact the law should not allow a personal declaration to override.

bank.q: Workers need stronger unions and rights, and fair-pay agreements should return.
bank.ctx: 'Fair-pay agreements' set industry-wide pay deals. This supports stronger unions and worker rights and bringing those agreements back.

bank.q: Union power and central pay deals hold the economy back and cost jobs.
bank.ctx: This argues union power and central pay deals hold the economy back and cost jobs.

bank.q: Benefits are too low and should be raised to lift people out of poverty.
bank.ctx: This argues welfare benefits are too low and should be raised to lift people out of poverty.

bank.q: Raising benefits too far just weakens the incentive to work.
bank.ctx: This argues raising benefits too far weakens the incentive to work.

bank.q: New Zealand over-regulates business; companies need far less red tape.
bank.ctx: This argues New Zealand over-regulates business and companies need far less red tape.

bank.q: Cutting regulation just lets companies off the hook on workers and the environment.
bank.ctx: This argues cutting regulation just lets companies off the hook on workers and the environment.

bank.q: The tighter gun laws passed after the Christchurch attack were right and should stay.
bank.ctx: After the 2019 Christchurch mosque attacks, NZ banned many semi-automatic weapons. This supports keeping those tighter gun laws.

bank.q: The post-Christchurch gun laws punished law-abiding owners and should be loosened.
bank.ctx: This argues the post-Christchurch gun laws punished law-abiding owners and should be loosened.

bank.q: Abortion is a settled right and access should be protected.
bank.ctx: This treats abortion as a settled right whose access should be protected. NZ decriminalised abortion in 2020.

bank.q: Abortion ends a human life and the law is too permissive.
bank.ctx: This argues abortion ends a human life and the current law is too permissive.

bank.q: The legalisation of assisted dying was the right, compassionate choice.
bank.ctx: NZ legalised assisted dying for the terminally ill in 2021. This defends that as the right, compassionate choice.

bank.q: Assisted dying puts pressure on the vulnerable and crosses a line society should not cross.
bank.ctx: This argues assisted dying pressures the vulnerable and crosses a line society shouldn't cross.

bank.q: Drug use should be treated as a health issue, and cannabis legalised.
bank.ctx: This supports treating drug use as a health issue and legalising cannabis.

bank.q: Going soft on drugs fuels addiction and harm, and it should be reversed.
bank.ctx: This argues softening drug laws fuels addiction and harm and should be reversed.

bank.q: New Zealand should take a harder line on China even at the cost of trade.
bank.ctx: This supports taking a harder line on China (a major power) even at the cost of trade.

bank.q: New Zealand’s prosperity depends on trade with China, and confrontation would be reckless.
bank.ctx: This argues New Zealand's prosperity depends on trade with China and confrontation would be reckless.

bank.q: New Zealand should increase defence spending and align more closely with allies like AUKUS.
bank.ctx: This supports higher defence spending and aligning more with allies, such as the AUKUS security pact.

bank.q: New Zealand should stay independent and nuclear-free, not be dragged into a military bloc.
bank.ctx: This argues NZ should stay independent and nuclear-free rather than be pulled into a military bloc.

bank.q: Protecting nature should take priority over new mining and development.
bank.ctx: This puts protecting nature ahead of new mining and development.

bank.q: Endless environmental objections are strangling the projects New Zealand needs to prosper.
bank.ctx: This argues endless environmental objections block the projects New Zealand needs.

bank.q: The government should intervene directly, with price controls, to ease the cost of living.
bank.ctx: This supports the government stepping in with price controls to ease the cost of living.

bank.q: Price controls just cause shortages; they don’t fix the cost of living.
bank.ctx: This argues price controls just cause shortages and don't fix the real problem.

bank.q: Major decisions should be put to the people directly through binding referendums.
bank.ctx: This supports direct democracy: putting major decisions to the public in binding referendums.

bank.q: Referendums reduce complex questions to slogans and are easily hijacked by populists.
bank.ctx: This argues referendums reduce complex issues to slogans and are easily hijacked by populists.

bank.q: Public media like RNZ and TVNZ are worth their funding and must stay independent.
bank.ctx: RNZ and TVNZ are New Zealand's public media. This argues they are worth their funding and must stay independent.

bank.q: Public broadcasters are biased and bloated, and their funding should be cut.
bank.ctx: This argues public broadcasters are biased and bloated and their funding should be cut.

bank.q: Immigrants should adapt to New Zealand culture, not the other way around.
bank.ctx: This argues immigrants should adapt to New Zealand's culture rather than the country adapting to them.

bank.q: A living culture is always a blend; demanding assimilation impoverishes New Zealand.
bank.ctx: This argues a living culture is always a blend, so demanding assimilation impoverishes New Zealand.

bank.q: Parents should have more control over what their children are taught about gender and identity.
bank.ctx: This argues parents should have more control over what schools teach their children about gender and identity.

bank.q: Curriculum should be set by educators and evidence, not by parental veto over inclusion.
bank.ctx: This argues the curriculum should be set by educators and evidence, not by a parental veto over inclusion.

bank.q: Free trade has made New Zealand richer and should be defended.
bank.ctx: This supports free trade as having made New Zealand richer.

bank.q: Free trade left New Zealand exposed and dependent, and communities behind.
bank.ctx: This argues free trade left New Zealand exposed, dependent, and with communities left behind.

bank.q: The unemployed are treated with too much suspicion; the safety net should be stronger.
bank.ctx: This argues the unemployed are treated with too much suspicion and the safety net should be stronger.

bank.q: Welfare too easily becomes a trap, and sanctions protect taxpayers who fund it.
bank.ctx: This argues welfare can trap people, and sanctions protect the taxpayers who fund it.

bank.q: New Zealanders should feel able to express national pride without being called racist.
bank.ctx: This argues New Zealanders should be able to express national pride without being accused of racism.

bank.q: Uncritical national pride glosses over colonisation and its ongoing harms.
bank.ctx: This argues uncritical national pride glosses over colonisation and its ongoing harms to Māori.

bank.q: Long-standing traditions carry the wisdom of generations and should not be discarded lightly.
bank.ctx: This is the conservative view of tradition: that long-standing customs and institutions hold accumulated wisdom, so we should be cautious about sweeping them away for something new.

bank.q: Worshipping tradition just lets the dead govern the living and blocks necessary change.
bank.ctx: This is the progressive reply: that clinging to tradition for its own sake lets the past dictate to the present and blocks change that is needed.

bank.q: A good society depends more on personal responsibility than on government support.
bank.ctx: This reflects a right-leaning value: that a good society rests mainly on individuals taking responsibility for their own lives, rather than leaning on government.

bank.q: Blaming individuals for problems the system creates is how the comfortable excuse others’ suffering.
bank.ctx: This reflects a left-leaning value: that many problems are caused by unfair systems, so blaming individuals lets the comfortable look past suffering they may benefit from.
